Value Example Result DateFormat_RU.Time 13:22 DateFormat_RU.TimeInWords 13 часов 22 минуты DateFormat_RU.TimeWithSeconds 13:22:32 DateFormat_RU.TimeWithSecondsInWords 13 часов 22 минуты 32 секунды DateFormat_RU.Year 2023 DateFormat_RU.YearShort 23 DateFormat_RU.YearWord 2023 год DateFormat_RU.DateAndTime 4 декабря 2023 13:22 DateFormat_RU.DateAndTimeShort 04.12.2023 13:25 DateFormat_RU.DateAndTimeShortWithSeconds 04.12.2023 13:25:32 DateFormat_RU.DateAndTimeWithSeconds 4 декабря 2023 13:22:32 DateFormat_RU.DateShort 04.12.2023 DateFormat_RU.FullDateYearAbbr 1 декабря 2023 г. DateFormat_RU.FullDateYearWord 1 декабря 2023 года DateFormat_RU.DateInWords первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третий год DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsYearGenitive первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третьего года DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsShort 1 декабря 2023 (первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третий) год DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsShortGenitive 1 декабря 2023 (первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третьего) год DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsFull 01.12.2023 (первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третий) год DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsFullGenitive 01.12.2023 (первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третьего) год DateFormat_RU.DateInWordsGenitive первого декабря две тысячи двадцать третьего года DateFormat_RU.DateQuoted "01" декабря 2023 г. DateFormat_RU.DateGuillemets «01» декабря 2023 г. DateFormat_RU.Day 01 DateFormat_RU.FullDateYearAbbrDay2 01 декабря 2023 г. DateFormat_RU.FullDateYearWordDay2 01 декабря 2023 года DateFormat_RU.DayMonth 01 декабря DateFormat_RU.Weekday Пятница DateFormat_RU.WeekdayShort Пт DateFormat_RU.Month декабрь DateFormat_RU.MonthYear декабрь 2023 DateFormat_RU.MonthShort дек DateFormat_RU.MonthNumber 12 DateFormat_RU.Minutes 22 DateFormat_RU.Seconds 32 DateFormat_RU.Hours 13

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
The function returns a text value in the selected format.

For example, suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.DateShort
)

Returns:

01.12.2023

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The selected format determines which part of the source value is included in the result.

For example, a field containing a date and time value can be used to extract only the date:

formatDate_RU(
    DateTime,
    DateFormat_RU.DateShort
)

Only the time:

formatDate_RU(
    DateTime,
    DateFormat_RU.Time
)

Or an individual date component, such as the year:

formatDate_RU(
    DateTime,
    DateFormat_RU.Year
)

The function does not change the original date or time value. It only controls how the value is displayed in the document.

Since formatDate_RU uses Russian date formatting, month names, weekday names, and dates written out in words are returned in Russian.

If the available formats do not meet your requirements, use a custom date-formatting function to define the desired date and time representation using a format mask.

docs.title: Date with Quotation Marks
docs.text:
Suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.DateGuillemets
)

Returns:

«01» декабря 2023 г.

docs.title: Date Written Out in Words
docs.text:
Suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.DateInWords
)

Returns:

первое декабря две тысячи двадцать третий год

docs.title: Extracting the Day of the Week
docs.text:
Suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.Weekday
)

Returns:

Пятница

docs.title: Extracting the Month
docs.text:
Suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.Month
)

Returns:

декабрь

docs.title: Extracting the Year
docs.text:
Suppose the ContractDate field contains:

01.12.2023

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    ContractDate,
    DateFormat_RU.Year
)

Returns:

2023

docs.title: Formatting Date and Time
docs.text:
Suppose the DateTime field contains:

04.12.2023 13:22:32

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    DateTime,
    DateFormat_RU.DateAndTimeWithSeconds
)

Returns:

4 декабря 2023 13:22:32

docs.title: Extracting Time Without Seconds
docs.text:
Suppose the DateTime field contains:

04.12.2023 13:22:32

The expression:

formatDate_RU(
    DateTime,
    DateFormat_RU.Time
)

Returns:

13:22

docs.title: Using with Other Functions
docs.text:
The Expression parameter can accept the result of another function, provided that it returns a date or time value.

For example, formatDate_RU can be used together with the date function:

formatDate_RU(
    date(1, 12, 2023),
    DateFormat_RU.FullDateYearWord
)

Returns:

1 декабря 2023 года

First, the date function creates a date value. The formatDate_RU function then converts it into the selected text format.

docs.title: formatFullName_RU
docs.text: The formatFullName_RU function formats a person's full name according to the specified format and grammatical case.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
formatFullName_RU(Expression for the name, Grammatical case, Format)

Parameters:

  • Expression for the name — required. The text value containing the person's full name.
  • Grammatical case — required. Specifies the grammatical case in which the full name should be displayed.
  • Format — required. Specifies which parts of the full name should be included and how they should be displayed.

The following values are available for the Grammatical case parameter:

Value Russian case questions GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative кто? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Genitive кого? чего? GrammaticalCase_RU.Dative кому? чему? GrammaticalCase_RU.Accusative кого? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Instrumental кем? чем? GrammaticalCase_RU.Prepositional о ком? о чём?

The following values are available for the Format parameter:

Value Result SurnameNamePatronymic Иванов Иван Иванович SurnameName Иванов Иван NamePatronymic Иван Иванович SurnameInitials Иванов И.И. InitialsSurname И.И. Иванов Surname Иванов Name Иван Patronymic Иванович

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
The function returns a text value containing the person's full name in the selected format and grammatical case.

For example, suppose the FullName field contains:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The expression:

formatFullName_RU(
    FullName,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative,
    FullNameFormat_RU.SurnameInitials
)

Returns:

Иванов И.И.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
When a grammatical case is specified, the function declines the parts of the full name included in the selected format.

For example, if the Surname format and Dative case are selected, the function returns the surname in the dative case.

If a full name is declined incorrectly, you can specify the required form using grammatical exceptions in the template-filling interface.

docs.title: Initials Before the Surname
docs.text:
Suppose the FullName field contains:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The expression:

formatFullName_RU(
    FullName,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative,
    FullNameFormat_RU.InitialsSurname
)

Returns:

И.И. Иванов

docs.title: Surname in the Dative Case
docs.text:
Suppose the FullName field contains:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The expression:

formatFullName_RU(
    FullName,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Dative,
    FullNameFormat_RU.Surname
)

Returns:

Иванову

docs.title: Name and Patronymic in the Genitive Case
docs.text:
Suppose the FullName field contains:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The expression:

formatFullName_RU(
    FullName,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Genitive,
    FullNameFormat_RU.NamePatronymic
)

Returns:

Ивана Ивановича

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All three parameters are required.

For example, the following expression is incomplete:

formatFullName_RU(
    FullName,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

The Format parameter is missing, so the expression will return an error when evaluated.

You must also use valid values for the Grammatical case and Format parameters.

docs.title: Using with Other Functions
docs.text:
The result of formatFullName_RU can be passed to other functions that process text.

For example, the upper function converts the formatted full name to uppercase:

upper(
    formatFullName_RU(
        FullName,
        GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative,
        FullNameFormat_RU.SurnameInitials
    )
)

Returns:

ИВАНОВ И.И.

docs.title: formatNumber
docs.text:
The formatNumber function changes how a numeric value is displayed.

It allows you to specify the number of decimal places, the decimal separator, and, if necessary, the thousands separator.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
formatNumber(number, "format", "decimalSeparator")

Parameters:

  • number — the numeric value to format;
  • format — defines how the number is displayed;
  • decimalSeparator — the character used to separate the fractional part from the integer part.

If necessary, you can also specify a thousands separator:

formatNumber(number, "format", "decimalSeparator", "thousandsSeparator")
  • thousandsSeparator — an optional parameter that defines the character used to separate groups of digits in the integer part.

In the function settings, the number format can be configured in two ways:

  • if Custom format is disabled — specify the number of Decimal places;
  • if Custom format is enabled — define the format string manually.

You can also specify:

  • Decimal separator — the character used to separate the fractional part from the integer part;
  • Thousands separator — the character used to separate groups of digits in the integer part. If no separator is required, select Empty.

docs.title: Custom format
docs.text:
When Custom format is enabled, the format string is created using special characters:

Symbol Description # Digit placeholder. Displays only significant digits. 0 Digit placeholder with zero padding. If there is no digit in this position, 0 is displayed. . Position of the decimal separator. Can appear only once in the format string. , Position of the thousands separator.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns the formatted numeric value as text.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The . and , characters in the format string define the positions of the separators. The actual characters displayed in the result are specified by Decimal separator and Thousands separator.

If the format contains fewer decimal places than the source value, the displayed value is rounded.

Because the function returns text, calculations with the number should be performed before applying formatNumber.

docs.title: Displaying two decimal places
docs.text:
Suppose the amount field contains:

125.6

Expression:

formatNumber(
    amount,
    "0.00",
    "."
)

returns:

125.60

docs.title: Adding a thousands separator
docs.text:
Suppose the amount field contains:

1234567.865464

Expression:

formatNumber(
    amount,
    "#,##0.00",
    ".",
    ","
)

returns:

1,234,567.87

docs.title: Displaying only significant decimal digits
docs.text:
Suppose the amount field contains:

125.5

Expression:

formatNumber(
    amount,
    "0.##",
    "."
)

returns:

125.5

If the amount field contains:

125

the same expression returns:

125

docs.title: integerToText
docs.text:
The integerToText function converts a number to its text representation.

The function supports both cardinal and ordinal numbers.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
integerToText(expression, format)

Parameters:

  • expression — a numeric value or expression to convert to text;
  • format — determines whether the number is converted to a cardinal or ordinal form.

The following values are available for format:

Value Number type Example NumberType.Cardinal Cardinal twenty-one NumberType.Ordinal Ordinal twenty-first

In the function settings:

  • Expression — specifies the number, field reference, or expression to convert;
  • Format — selects Cardinal or Ordinal.

If a decimal number is passed to the function, only its integer part is used. The fractional part is discarded without rounding.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the text representation of the number.

For example:

integerToText(
    21,
    NumberType.Cardinal
)

returns:

twenty-one

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The function converts only the numeric value. It does not add units of measurement, currency names, or other text.

If a decimal value needs to be converted in full, its integer and fractional parts should be processed separately.

docs.title: Cardinal number
docs.text:
Expression:

integerToText(
    1234,
    NumberType.Cardinal
)

returns:

one thousand two hundred thirty-four

docs.title: Ordinal number
docs.text:
Expression:

integerToText(
    21,
    NumberType.Ordinal
)

returns:

twenty-first

docs.title: Decimal number
docs.text:
Suppose the amount field contains:

1234.56

Expression:

integerToText(
    amount,
    NumberType.Cardinal
)

returns:

one thousand two hundred thirty-four

The fractional part .56 is not included in the result.

docs.title: Amount in US dollars and cents
docs.text:
Suppose the amount field contains:

1234.56

To display the integer and fractional parts separately as US dollars and cents, use:

integerToText(
    amount,
    NumberType.Cardinal
) & " " &
if(
    amount - (amount mod 1) = 1,
    "US dollar",
    "US dollars"
) & " " &
integerToText(
    round((amount mod 1) * 100, 0),
    NumberType.Cardinal
) & " " &
if(
    round((amount mod 1) * 100, 0) = 1,
    "cent",
    "cents"
)

Result:

one thousand two hundred thirty-four US dollars fifty-six cents

Here:

  • amount mod 1 — returns the fractional part of the number;
  • (amount mod 1) * 100 — converts the fractional part to cents;
  • round(..., 0) — rounds the number of cents to an integer;
  • amount - (amount mod 1) — returns the integer part used to select US dollar or US dollars;
  • if(...) — selects the singular or plural currency name.

docs.title: integerToText_RU
docs.text:
The integerToText_RU function displays an integer in digits and/or words and adjusts the grammatical form of a specified word to agree with the number.

For example, the number 3 and the word документ can be displayed as:

3 (три) документа

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
integerToText_RU(Number expression, Expression of the word, Custom format, Numeral type, Grammatical case, Thousands separator)

Parameters:

  • Number expression — required. The integer value to be formatted.
  • Expression of the word — required. The word that must agree with the number.
  • Custom format — required. Specifies how the number and word are displayed.
  • Numeral type — required. Specifies whether a cardinal or ordinal numeral is used.
  • Grammatical case — optional. Specifies the grammatical case in which the numeral and word are displayed.
  • Thousands separator — optional. Specifies the character used to separate digit groups in the numeric representation.

docs.title: Custom Format
docs.text:
The custom format string determines the content and order of the result.

The following symbols are supported:

Symbol Description i Number in digits ii Number written out in words W Word in the appropriate grammatical form

For example, if the number is 3 and the word is "документ":

Format Result "i W" 3 документа "ii W" три документа "i (ii) W" 3 (три) документа

Spaces and punctuation marks in the format string are preserved in the result.

Alphabetic characters other than the supported format symbols are ignored. To include text that must remain unchanged, enclose it in single quotation marks (').

Double quotation marks (") are not allowed inside the custom format itself.

docs.title: Numeral Type
docs.text:
The following options are available for the Numeral type parameter:

  • Cardinal — a cardinal numeral indicating quantity.
  • Ordinal — an ordinal numeral indicating position or order.

docs.title: Grammatical Case
docs.text:
The following values are available for the Grammatical case parameter:

Value Russian case questions GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative кто? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Genitive кого? чего? GrammaticalCase_RU.Dative кому? чему? GrammaticalCase_RU.Accusative кого? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Instrumental кем? чем? GrammaticalCase_RU.Prepositional о ком? о чём?

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: The function returns a text value formatted according to the specified parameters.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The grammatical form of the word is determined automatically based on the number and the specified grammatical case.

For example, the function selects the appropriate form of the word "документ":

  • 1 документ
  • 2 документа
  • 5 документов

The thousands separator applies to the numeric representation of the number (i).

docs.title: Number in Digits and Words
docs.text:
Suppose the DocumentCount field contains:

3

The expression:

integerToText_RU(
    DocumentCount,
    "документ",
    "i (ii) W",
    NumeralType_RU.Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

Returns:

3 (три) документа

docs.title: Number Written Out in Words
docs.text:
Suppose the DocumentCount field contains:

5

The expression:

integerToText_RU(
    DocumentCount,
    "документ",
    "ii W",
    NumeralType_RU.Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

Returns:

пять документов

docs.title: Changing the Grammatical Case
docs.text:
Suppose the DocumentCount field contains:

3

The expression:

integerToText_RU(
    DocumentCount,
    "документ",
    "i (ii) W",
    NumeralType_RU.Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Genitive
)

Returns:

3 (трёх) документов

docs.title: Using a Thousands Separator
docs.text:
Suppose the DocumentCount field contains:

1250

The expression:

integerToText_RU(
    DocumentCount,
    "документ",
    "i W",
    NumeralType_RU.Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative,
    " "
)

Returns:

1 250 документов

docs.title: numberToText_RU
docs.text: The numberToText_RU function displays a number together with a word in the appropriate grammatical form.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
numberToText_RU(Number expression, Expression of the word, Format, Numeral type, Grammatical case)

Parameters:

  • Number expression — an integer or decimal numeric value.
  • Expression of the word — the word that must agree with the number.
  • Format — specifies how the number is displayed.
  • Numeral type — specifies the type of numeral.
  • Grammatical case — specifies the grammatical case in which the numeral and word are returned.

The following options are available for the Format parameter:

Value Result Long 5 (пять) комнат Short 5 комнат InWords пять комнат

The following options are available for the Numeral type parameter:

  • Cardinal — a cardinal numeral indicating quantity.
  • Ordinal — an ordinal numeral indicating position or order.

The following values are available for the Grammatical case parameter:

Value Russian case questions GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative кто? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Genitive кого? чего? GrammaticalCase_RU.Dative кому? чему? GrammaticalCase_RU.Accusative кого? что? GrammaticalCase_RU.Instrumental кем? чем? GrammaticalCase_RU.Prepositional о ком? о чём?

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: The function returns a text value in which the number and the specified word agree according to the selected parameters.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The function supports both integer and decimal values.

The grammatical form of the word is determined automatically based on the numeric value and the specified grammatical case.

Unlike the integerToText_RU function, numberToText_RU allows you to select the output format from predefined options.

docs.title: Number in Digits and Words
docs.text:
Suppose the Quantity field contains:

5

The expression:

numberToText_RU(
    Quantity,
    "комната",
    Long,
    Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

Returns:

5 (пять) комнат

docs.title: Short Format
docs.text:
Suppose the Quantity field contains:

2

The expression:

numberToText_RU(
    Quantity,
    "документ",
    Short,
    Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

Returns:

2 документа

docs.title: Number Written Out in Words
docs.text:
Suppose the Quantity field contains:

3

The expression:

numberToText_RU(
    Quantity,
    "этаж",
    InWords,
    Cardinal,
    GrammaticalCase_RU.Nominative
)

Returns:

три этажа

docs.title: transliterate_RU
docs.text: The transliterate_RU function converts Cyrillic text into Latin characters.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
transliterate_RU(Value)

Parameters:

  • Value — required. The text value to be transliterated into Latin characters.

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: The function returns a text value in which Cyrillic letters are replaced with their corresponding Latin characters.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Transliteration is performed character by character. The capitalization of the original text is preserved.

For example:

Cyrillic Latin Ж Zh Ю Iu Я Ia Й I

docs.title: Transliterating a Full Name
docs.text:
Suppose the FullName field contains:

Петрова Ирина Сергеевна

The expression:

transliterate_RU(FullName)

Returns:

Petrova Irina Sergeevna

docs.title: Using with Other Functions
docs.text:
The transliterate_RU function can be used as an argument in other functions that process text.

For example, to transliterate a value and convert the result to lowercase:

lower(transliterate_RU(FullName))

Suppose the FullName field contains:

Петрова Ирина Сергеевна

The result is:

petrova irina sergeevna

docs.title: wordEnding_RU
docs.text: The wordEnding_RU function inserts the appropriate word ending depending on the gender and number of the value in a text field.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
wordEnding_RU(Expression of the word, Masculine gender, Feminine gender, Neuter gender, Plural)

Parameters:

  • Expression of the word — the identifier of the text field whose value is used to determine gender and number.
  • Masculine gender — the ending for the masculine gender.
  • Feminine gender — the ending for the feminine gender.
  • Neuter gender — the ending for the neuter gender.
  • Plural — the ending for the plural form.

Endings must be specified in double quotation marks.

For example:

wordEnding_RU(FullName, "ый", "ая", "ое", "ые")
Field value Returned ending Masculine gender ый Feminine gender ая Neuter gender ое Plural ые

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
The function returns one of the specified text endings.

For example, if the FullName field contains the full name of a man:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The expression:

wordEnding_RU(FullName, "ый", "ая", "ое", "ые")

Returns:

ый

docs.title: Salutation by Full Name
docs.text:
Expression:

"Уважаем" & wordEnding_RU(FullName, "ый", "ая", "ое", "ые")

If the FullName field contains:

Иванов Иван Иванович

The result is:

Уважаемый

If the FullName field contains:

Иванова Анна Сергеевна

The result is:

Уважаемая

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The value used to determine gender and number must contain text suitable for morphological analysis.

If it contains digits, quotation marks, or punctuation marks, the function may fail to determine the correct form or may return an error.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
The index function returns a list item by its position.

List positions start at 1: the first item has position 1, the second has position 2, and so on.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
For a list with simple items:

index(list, position)

Parameters:

  • list — the identifier of the list field from which the item should be retrieved;
  • position — the position of the item. You can specify a number or an expression that returns a position.

For example:

index(stages, 2)

returns the second item from the stages list.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the identifier of the required nested field after the function using dot notation:

index(list, position).field

For example:

index(products, 2).name

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • 2 — the item position;
  • name — the nested field identifier.

docs.title: Getting an item by position
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

stages

The list contains:

Position Value 1 Preparation 2 Approval 3 Signing

The expression:

index(stages, 2)

returns:

Approval

Here:

  • stages — the list field identifier;
  • 2 — the item position in the list.

docs.title: Getting a field from the first item that matches a condition
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each list item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — the identifier of the product name field;
  • price — the identifier of the product price field.

The list contains:

Position name price 1 Chair 3500 2 Desk 7500 3 Cabinet 12000

You need to get the name of the first product with a price greater than 5000.

Expression:

index(
    products,
    match(
        product in products,
        product.price > 5000
    )
).name

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier in the template;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the match function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • match(...) — returns the position of the first matching item;
  • index(...) — returns the item at that position;
  • name — the field of the matching item whose value should be returned.

The match function checks the items in order:

3500 > 5000 → false
7500 > 5000 → true

The second item is the first one that matches the condition, so the expression effectively becomes:

index(products, 2).name

Result:

Desk

docs.title: Getting a value from the last item in a list
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

payments

Each list item is a Struct field containing:

balance

You need to get the balance value from the last item in the list, while the number of items is not known in advance.

Expression:

index(
    payments,
    count(payment in payments)
).balance

Here:

  • payments — the list field identifier;
  • payment — the name of the current item defined inside the count function;
  • count(...) — returns the number of items in the list;
  • the returned value is used as the position of the last item;
  • balance — the nested field identifier whose value should be returned.

If the list contains four items:

count(payment in payments)

returns:

4

The expression then effectively becomes:

index(payments, 4).balance

and returns the balance value from the last item in the list.

docs.title: avg
docs.text:
The avg function calculates the arithmetic mean of numeric values from list items.

A numeric field or an expression can be used as the value for the calculation.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
avg(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the current list item;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • expression — a numeric value or expression whose result is included in the arithmetic mean calculation.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If each list item is a Struct field, you can assign any valid name to the current item and use it to access nested fields.

For example:

avg(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined directly in the function;
  • price — the nested numeric field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used to calculate the arithmetic mean.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. For example, instead of product, you can use item:

avg(item in products, item.price)

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains simple numeric values, the current item itself is used in the expression.

Suppose the ratings list contains numeric values.

Expression:

avg(rating in ratings, rating)

In this case, each value in the list is used directly in the calculation.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns a number — the arithmetic mean of the expression results for all items in the list.

docs.title: Calculating the average product price
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

The list contains:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

To calculate the average product price, use:

avg(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the avg function;
  • price — the numeric field identifier inside the item;
  • product.price — the value retrieved from each list item.

Result:

7100

docs.title: Calculating the average of a simple numeric list
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

ratings

The list contains:

4
5
3
5

Expression:

avg(rating in ratings, rating)

returns:

4.25

docs.title: Calculating the average result of an expression
docs.text:
The second parameter can also contain an expression.

Suppose the products list contains:

  • name — product name;
  • price — unit price;
  • quantity — product quantity.

Source data:

name price quantity Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 5 Printer 12000 1 Mouse 600 10

You need to calculate the average total cost of a product line based on its quantity.

Expression:

avg(product in products, product.price * product.quantity)

For each item, the function first calculates the line total:

name Calculation Value Monitor 15000 × 2 30000 Keyboard 800 × 5 4000 Printer 12000 × 1 12000 Mouse 600 × 10 6000

The function then calculates the arithmetic mean of these values.

Result:

13000

docs.title: count
docs.text: The count function determines the number of items in a list.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
count(item in list)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function;
  • list — the identifier of the list field whose items should be counted.

For example:

count(product in products)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier in the template;
  • product — the name of the list item defined directly in the function.

You can choose the item name yourself. It is used only inside the function expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns an integer — the number of items in the list.

docs.title: Counting list items
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

The list contains:

Position Name 1 Monitor 2 Keyboard 3 Printer 4 Mouse

Expression:

count(product in products)

returns:

4

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the list item defined inside the count function.

docs.title: Counting items that match a condition
docs.text:
The count function can be applied to a list returned by filter.

Suppose the products list contains:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

You need to determine how many products have a price greater than 5000.

Expression:

count(
    product in filter(
        item in products,
        item.price > 5000
    )
)

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • item — the name of the current item inside the filter function;
  • item.price > 5000 — the filtering condition;
  • filter(...) — returns a new list containing only matching products;
  • product — the name of an item in the filtered list inside the count function.

After filtering, the list contains:

Monitor — 15000
Printer — 12000

Therefore, count returns:

2

docs.title: Getting the last item in a list
docs.text:
The result of count can be used as an item position in the index function.

Suppose the template contains a list field:

payments

Each list item contains the following field:

balance

You need to get the balance value from the last item in the list, while the number of items is not known in advance.

Expression:

index(
    payments,
    count(payment in payments)
).balance

Here:

  • payments — the list field identifier;
  • payment — the name of the list item inside the count function;
  • count(...) — returns the number of items in the list;
  • the returned number is used by index as the position of the last item;
  • balance — the nested field identifier whose value should be returned.

For example, if the list contains four items:

count(payment in payments)

returns:

4

The expression then effectively becomes:

index(payments, 4).balance

and returns the balance value from the last item in the list.

docs.title: filter
docs.text: The filter function selects list items that match a specified condition.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
filter(item in list, condition)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the condition;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • condition — a Boolean expression that determines whether the current item should be included in the result.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

For example:

filter(product in products, product.price > 5000)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price > 5000 — the filtering condition.

Only products with a price greater than 5000 are included in the result.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a new list containing only the items for which the condition returns true.

The original list is not changed.

The result of filter(...) can be used instead of the original list:

  • in a for or t_for block;
  • in other list functions;
  • in aggregate functions such as count, sum, avg, min, and max.

This allows you to filter the required items first and then perform calculations only on those items.

docs.title: Outputting only matching list items
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each item contains:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

Source list:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

You need to output only products with a price greater than 5000.

{for(item in filter(product in products, product.price > 5000))}
{item.name} — {item.price}
{/for}

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the filter function;
  • product.price > 5000 — the filtering condition;
  • filter(...) — returns a new list containing only matching products;
  • item — the name of the current item in the filtered list inside the for block.

Result:

Monitor — 15000
Printer — 12000

The original products list remains unchanged.

docs.title: Calculating a sum for a filtered list
docs.text:
The result of filter can be passed directly to an aggregate function.

Suppose the products list contains:

name price quantity Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 5 Printer 12000 1 Mouse 600 10

You need to calculate the total cost only for products whose unit price is greater than 5000.

First, filter selects the matching items:

filter(product in products, product.price > 5000)

The resulting list contains:

name price quantity Monitor 15000 2 Printer 12000 1

The filtered list can then be passed directly to sum:

sum(
    item in filter(
        product in products,
        product.price > 5000
    ),
    item.price * item.quantity
)

Here:

  • product — the name of the source list item inside filter;
  • filter(...) — returns a list of products with a price greater than 5000;
  • item — the name of the filtered list item inside sum;
  • item.price * item.quantity — the value calculated for each item and included in the sum.

The calculation uses:

15000 × 2 = 30000
12000 × 1 = 12000

The function returns:

42000

In the same way, a filtered list can be passed to count, avg, min, or max when a calculation needs to be performed only for items that match a specified condition.

docs.title: group
docs.text: The group function combines list items into groups based on the same value of a specified property or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
group(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. In the function settings, this parameter is Item list name;
  • list — the identifier of the list field. In the function settings, this parameter is List;
  • expression — the property or expression used to group the items. In the function settings, this parameter is Grouping property.

The item name can be chosen freely and is used only inside the function.

For example:

group(product in products, product.category)

Here:

  • product — the current item name specified in Item list name;
  • products — the list field identifier specified in List;
  • category — the nested field identifier;
  • product.category — the value specified in Grouping property.

Items with the same category value are placed in the same group.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a list of groups.

Each group automatically provides two properties:

  • .Key — the value used to create the group;
  • .List — the list of source items included in the group.

For example, if the current group is named groupItem:

groupItem.Key
groupItem.List

You can choose the name groupItem yourself.

The .Key and .List properties are created by the group function and must be specified exactly as shown. They are not field identifiers from the form.

The resulting groupItem.List can be used like any other list. For example, you can iterate through it in a for block or pass it to sum, count, avg, min, or max.

docs.title: Grouping products and calculating a subtotal for each group
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each list item contains:

  • name — product name;
  • category — product category;
  • price — unit price;
  • quantity — product quantity.

Source list:

name category price quantity Monitor Electronics 15000 2 Printer Electronics 12000 1 Desk Furniture 20000 1 Chair Furniture 5000 4

The products need to be grouped by category. For each category, the products should be displayed and their total cost calculated.

Use an outer for block to iterate through the result of group and an inner for block to iterate through the items in each group:

{for(groupItem in group(product in products, product.category))}
{groupItem.Key}

{for(item in groupItem.List)}
{item.name} — {item.quantity} × {item.price}
{/for}

Total: {sum(totalItem in groupItem.List, totalItem.price * totalItem.quantity)}

{/for}

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • product — the current item name specified in Item list name;
  • product.category — the value specified in Grouping property;
  • groupItem — the name of the current group in the outer for block;
  • groupItem.Key — the current category;
  • groupItem.List — the products included in the current category;
  • item — the name of the current product in the inner for block;
  • totalItem — the name of the current product inside the sum function;
  • totalItem.price * totalItem.quantity — the product line total used to calculate the subtotal.

For the Electronics group, sum calculates:

15000 × 2 + 12000 × 1 = 42000

For the Furniture group:

20000 × 1 + 5000 × 4 = 40000

The result is:

Electronics

Monitor — 2 × 15000
Printer — 1 × 12000

Total: 42000


Furniture

Desk — 1 × 20000
Chair — 4 × 5000

Total: 40000

docs.title: match
docs.text: The match function finds the first list item that satisfies a specified condition and returns its position.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
match(item in list, condition)

Parameters:

  • item — the current list item used in the condition;
  • list — the list in which the search is performed;
  • condition — a Boolean expression that determines whether the current item matches. The condition must return true or false.

docs.title: List with a Struct item
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, you can assign any valid name to the current item and use it to access nested fields.

For example:

match(
    product in products,
    product.price > 5000
)

Here:

  • product — the name of the current list item;
  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product.price — the price field of the current Struct item.

The current item name is used only inside the function expression. For example, instead of product, you can use item, position, _1, or another valid name:

match(
    position in products,
    position.price > 5000
)

docs.title: List with a simple item
docs.text:
If the list contains simple values, such as text or numbers, the condition is applied directly to the current item.

For example, for a list of numbers:

match(
    number in numbers,
    number >= 5
)

The function finds the position of the first value greater than or equal to 5.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns an integer — the position of the first list item for which the condition returns true.

List positions start at 1.

If no item matches the condition, the function does not return a position.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The search starts from the beginning of the list. If several items match the condition, only the position of the first matching item is returned.

The function returns the item position, not the item itself or the value of one of its fields.

docs.title: Finding the first product with a price greater than 5,000
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each item in products is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

For example:

Position name price 1 Chair 3500 2 Desk 7500 3 Cabinet 12000

To find the position of the first product with a price greater than 5000, use:

match(
    product in products,
    product.price > 5000
)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier in the template;
  • product — the name assigned to the current list item;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price — the price value of the current item.

The function checks the items in order:

3500 > 5000 → false
7500 > 5000 → true

The second item is the first one that matches the condition, so the function returns:

2

docs.title: Finding a value in a list of numbers
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

numbers

The list contains:

2
4
7
9

To find the position of the first value greater than or equal to 5, use:

match(
    number in numbers,
    number >= 5
)

Here:

  • number — the name assigned to the current list item;
  • numbers — the list field identifier;
  • number >= 5 — the condition checked for each item.

The function checks the values in order:

2 >= 5 → false
4 >= 5 → false
7 >= 5 → true

The first matching value is in the third position, so the function returns:

3

docs.title: Using with other functions
docs.text:
The result of match can be passed to the index function to retrieve the matching list item or one of its fields.

For example, to get the name of the first product with a price greater than 5000:

index(
    products,
    match(
        product in products,
        product.price > 5000
    )
).name

For the following list:

Position name price 1 Chair 3500 2 Desk 7500 3 Cabinet 12000

the expression returns:

Desk

First, match finds the position of the first matching item. Then index retrieves the name field from that item.

docs.title: max
docs.text: The max function determines the maximum numeric value in a list.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
max(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the expression;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • expression — a numeric value or expression whose maximum result should be determined.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains numeric values, use the current item in the expression.

For example:

max(number in numberList, number)

Here:

  • numberList — the list field identifier;
  • number — the name of the current list item;
  • the second number — the value used to determine the maximum.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the required numeric field in the expression.

For example:

max(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item;
  • price — the nested numeric field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used to determine the maximum.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns the maximum result of the expression across all items in the list.

docs.title: Finding the maximum product price
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

Source data:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

Expression:

max(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the max function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used in the comparison.

The function returns:

15000

The function returns the maximum price value, not the Monitor list item itself.

docs.title: Finding the maximum result of an expression
docs.text:
The second parameter can also contain an expression.

Suppose the products list also contains the following field:

quantity

Source data:

name price quantity Chair 3500 4 Desk 7500 1 Cabinet 12000 2

You need to determine the maximum total cost of a product line based on its quantity.

Expression:

max(product in products, product.price * product.quantity)

For each item, the function calculates:

name Calculation Result Chair 3500 × 4 14000 Desk 7500 × 1 7500 Cabinet 12000 × 2 24000

The function returns:

24000

docs.title: min
docs.text: The min function determines the minimum numeric value in a list.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
min(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the expression;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • expression — a numeric value or expression whose minimum result should be determined.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains numeric values, use the current item in the expression.

For example:

min(number in numberList, number)

Here:

  • numberList — the list field identifier;
  • number — the name of the current list item;
  • the second number — the value used to determine the minimum.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the required numeric field in the expression.

For example:

min(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item;
  • price — the nested numeric field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used to determine the minimum.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns the minimum result of the expression across all items in the list.

docs.title: Finding the minimum product price
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

Source data:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

Expression:

min(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the min function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used in the comparison.

The function compares:

15000
800
12000
600

and returns:

600

The function returns the minimum price value, not the Mouse list item itself.

docs.title: Finding the minimum result of an expression
docs.text:
The second parameter can also contain an expression.

Suppose the products list also contains the following field:

quantity

Source data:

name price quantity Chair 3500 4 Desk 7500 1 Cabinet 12000 2

You need to determine the minimum total cost of a product line based on its quantity.

Expression:

min(product in products, product.price * product.quantity)

For each item, the function first calculates:

name Calculation Result Chair 3500 × 4 14000 Desk 7500 × 1 7500 Cabinet 12000 × 2 24000

The function returns:

7500

docs.title: sort
docs.text: The sort function returns a copy of a list with its items arranged in ascending order.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sort(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the sorting expression;
  • list — the identifier of the list field whose items should be sorted;
  • expression — the value used to determine the order of the items.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains simple values, sorting can be performed by the value of the current item.

For example:

sort(number in numberList, number)

Here:

  • numberList — the list field identifier;
  • number — the name of the current list item;
  • the second number — the value used for sorting.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the nested field to sort by.

For example:

sort(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current list item;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used for sorting.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a sorted copy of the original list.

The original list is not changed.

To output the sorted items in a document, use the result of sort inside a for block.

docs.title: Sorting a list of numbers
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

numberList

It contains:

Position Value 1 8 2 3 3 12 4 5

To output the values in ascending order, use sort inside a for block:

{for(number in sort(item in numberList, item))}
{number}
{/for}

Here:

  • numberList — the identifier of the source list field;
  • item — the name of the current item inside the sort function;
  • the second item — the value used for sorting;
  • sort(...) — returns a sorted copy of the list;
  • number — the name of the current item in the sorted list inside the for block.

Result:

3
5
8
12

The original numberList remains unchanged.

docs.title: Sorting products by price
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — the product name field identifier;
  • price — the product price field identifier.

Source list:

Position name price 1 Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 3 Printer 12000 4 Mouse 600

To output the products in ascending order by price:

{for(item in sort(product in products, product.price))}
{item.name} — {item.price}
{/for}

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the sort function;
  • product.price — the value used for sorting;
  • sort(...) — returns a copy of products with the items in a different order;
  • item — the name of the current item in the sorted list inside the for block;
  • item.name and item.price — the fields of the current item.

Result:

Mouse — 600
Keyboard — 800
Printer — 12000
Monitor — 15000

docs.title: Sorting by the result of an expression
docs.text:
An expression can also be used as the sorting criterion.

Suppose the products list also contains the following field:

quantity

Source data:

name price quantity Chair 3500 4 Desk 7500 1 Cabinet 12000 2

The products need to be sorted by the total cost of each line — price × quantity.

Expression:

{for(item in sort(product in products, product.price * product.quantity))}
{item.name}
{/for}

For each item, the function calculates the expression value:

name Calculation Sorting value Chair 3500 × 4 14000 Desk 7500 × 1 7500 Cabinet 12000 × 2 24000

Result:

Desk
Chair
Cabinet

The calculated value is used only to determine the item order and is not added to the original list.

docs.title: sortDescending
docs.text: The sortDescending function returns a copy of a list with its items arranged in descending order.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sortDescending(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the sorting expression;
  • list — the identifier of the list field whose items should be sorted;
  • expression — the value used to determine the order of the items.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains simple values, sorting is performed by the value of the current item.

For example:

sortDescending(number in numberList, number)

Here:

  • numberList — the list field identifier;
  • number — the name of the current list item;
  • the second number — the value used for sorting.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the nested field to sort by.

For example:

sortDescending(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current list item;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used for sorting.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a sorted copy of the original list.

The original list is not changed.

To output the sorted items in a document, use the result of sortDescending inside a for block.

docs.title: Sorting a list of numbers
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

numberList

It contains:

Position Value 1 8 2 3 3 12 4 5

To output the values in descending order, use sortDescending inside a for block:

{for(number in sortDescending(item in numberList, item))}
{number}
{/for}

Here:

  • numberList — the identifier of the source list field;
  • item — the name of the current item inside the sortDescending function;
  • the second item — the value used for sorting;
  • sortDescending(...) — returns a sorted copy of the list;
  • number — the name of the current item in the sorted list inside the for block.

Result:

12
8
5
3

The original numberList remains unchanged.

docs.title: Sorting products by price in a table loop
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — the product name field identifier;
  • price — the product price field identifier.

Source list:

Position name price 1 Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 3 Printer 12000 4 Mouse 600

To output the products in a table from the highest price to the lowest, use sortDescending inside a t_for block:

{t_for(item in sortDescending(product in products, product.price))}
{item.name} | {item.price}
{/t_for}

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the sortDescending function;
  • product.price — the value used for sorting;
  • sortDescending(...) — returns a copy of the list with its items arranged by price in descending order;
  • item — the name of the current item in the sorted list inside the t_for block;
  • item.name and item.price — the fields whose values are output in the cells of the repeated row.

The table rows will be arranged as follows:

Name Price Monitor 15000 Printer 12000 Keyboard 800 Mouse 600

The original products list keeps its original item order.

docs.title: Sorting by the result of an expression
docs.text:
An expression can also be used as the sorting criterion.

Suppose the products list also contains the following field:

quantity

Source data:

name price quantity Chair 3500 4 Desk 7500 1 Cabinet 12000 2

The products need to be sorted by the total cost of each line in descending order:

price × quantity

Expression:

{for(item in sortDescending(product in products, product.price * product.quantity))}
{item.name}
{/for}

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the sortDescending function;
  • price and quantity — nested field identifiers;
  • product.price * product.quantity — the expression whose result is used for sorting;
  • item — the name of the current item in the sorted list inside the for block.

For each item, the function calculates:

name Calculation Sorting value Chair 3500 × 4 14000 Desk 7500 × 1 7500 Cabinet 12000 × 2 24000

Result:

Cabinet
Chair
Desk

The calculated value is used only to determine the item order and does not change the data in the original list.

docs.title: sum
docs.text: The sum function calculates the sum of numeric values from list items.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sum(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the expression;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • expression — a numeric value or expression whose results should be added together.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains numeric values, use the current item in the expression.

For example:

sum(number in numberList, number)

Here:

  • numberList — the list field identifier;
  • number — the name of the current list item;
  • the second number — the value included in the sum.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the required numeric field in the expression.

For example:

sum(product in products, product.quantity)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item;
  • quantity — the nested numeric field identifier;
  • product.quantity — the value included in the sum.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns the sum of the expression results for all items in the list.

docs.title: Calculating the total quantity of products
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • quantity — product quantity.

Source data:

name quantity Monitor 2 Keyboard 5 Printer 1 Mouse 10

To calculate the total quantity of products, use:

sum(product in products, product.quantity)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item inside the sum function;
  • quantity — the nested field identifier;
  • product.quantity — the value added to the total.

The function adds:

2 + 5 + 1 + 10

and returns:

18

docs.title: Calculating the total cost of products
docs.text:
The second parameter can also contain an expression.

Suppose the products list contains:

  • name — product name;
  • price — unit price;
  • quantity — product quantity.

Source data:

name price quantity Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 5 Printer 12000 1 Mouse 600 10

To calculate the total cost of all products:

sum(product in products, product.price * product.quantity)

For each item, the function first calculates the line total:

name Calculation Result Monitor 15000 × 2 30000 Keyboard 800 × 5 4000 Printer 12000 × 1 12000 Mouse 600 × 10 6000

The function then adds the calculated values:

30000 + 4000 + 12000 + 6000

Result:

52000

docs.title: if
docs.text:
The if function returns one of two values depending on whether a specified condition is met.

The function is useful when the result should change depending on a field value, comparison, or logical condition.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
if(condition, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse)

Parameters:

  • condition — the condition that determines the function result. Required;
  • valueIfTrue — the value returned if the condition is true. Required;
  • valueIfFalse — the value returned if the condition is false. Required.

The return values can be:

  • text;
  • numbers;
  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions;
  • null.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
If the condition is true, the function returns valueIfTrue. If the condition is false, it returns valueIfFalse.

For example:

if(quantity > 10, 100, 50)

If quantity is greater than 10, the result is:

100

Otherwise:

50

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
You can use a Boolean field as the condition:

if(delivery, "Delivery required", "Delivery not required")

If delivery = true, the function returns Delivery required. If delivery = false, it returns Delivery not required.

You can also build a condition using comparisons and logical operations.

For example:

if(
    amount >= 50000 и amount <= 100000,
    "Medium deal",
    "Other range"
)

For more information about comparisons, logical operations, and expressions, see Syntax.

The numeric value 1 can also be used as a true condition:

if(1, "Yes", "No")

Result:

Yes

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Returning field values

if(
    delivery,
    priceWithDelivery,
    priceWithoutDelivery
)

The function returns one of the two field values depending on the value of delivery.

Using another function

if(
    delivery,
    upper(deliveryMethod),
    "Pickup"
)

If delivery is required, the function returns the result of upper. Otherwise, it returns Pickup.

Returning an empty value

if(delivery, "Delivery", null)

If the condition is false, the function returns null.

Nested conditions

You can use if inside another if function:

if(
    amount > 100000,
    "Large",
    if(
        amount > 50000,
        "Medium",
        "Standard"
    )
)

Depending on the value of amount, the function returns Large, Medium, or Standard.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All three parameters are required.

For example:

if(delivery, "Yes")

returns an error because the third parameter is missing.

An error also occurs if the supplied condition cannot be processed by the function.

For example:

if("text", "Yes", "No")

returns an error.

docs.title: exp
docs.text:
The exp function raises the number e to the specified power.

The function is useful for calculations that use exponential values.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
exp(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the exponent. Required.

You can use:

  • a number;
  • a numeric field value;
  • a text value containing a number;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the result of raising e to the specified power.

For example:

exp(2)

Result:

7.38905609893065

If the value is 0:

exp(0)

Result:

1

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a negative value

exp(-1)

Result:

0.36787944117144233

Using a decimal value

exp(1.5)

Result:

4.4816890703380645

Using a field value and an expression

If the value field contains:

2

the expression:

exp(value + 1)

returns:

20.085536923187668

Using the result of another function

exp(round(1.6, 0))

Result:

7.38905609893065

Using a text representation of a number

exp("2")

Result:

7.38905609893065

The text value must contain a number that the function can use in the calculation.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The value parameter is required.

For example:

exp()

returns an error.

An error also occurs if a field passed to the function is empty.

docs.title: ln
docs.text: The ln function calculates the natural logarithm of a specified number.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
ln(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the value for which the natural logarithm should be calculated. Required.

You can use:

  • a number;
  • a numeric field value;
  • a text value containing a number;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the natural logarithm of the specified number.

For example:

ln(2)

Result:

0.6931471805599453

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a text representation of a number

ln("2")

Result:

0.6931471805599453

The text value must contain a number that the function can use in the calculation.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The value parameter is required.

For example:

ln()

returns an error.

An error also occurs if a field passed to the function is empty.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The ln function is the inverse of exp.

For example:

ln(exp(2))

Result:

2

docs.title: log10
docs.text: The log10 function calculates the base-10 logarithm of a specified number.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
log10(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the value for which the base-10 logarithm should be calculated. Required.

You can use:

  • a number;
  • a numeric field value;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the base-10 logarithm of the specified number.

For example:

log10(100)

Result:

2

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value

If the value field contains:

1000

the expression:

log10(value)

returns:

3

Using an expression

log10(10 * 10)

Result:

2

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The log10 function calculates a logarithm with base 10, while ln calculates the natural logarithm.

For example:

log10(100)

returns:

2

because:

10² = 100

docs.title: round
docs.text: The round function rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
round(value, decimalPlaces)

Parameters:

  • value — the numeric value to round. Required;
  • decimalPlaces — the number of decimal places to round to. Required.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

The function does not process text values or values from text fields as numbers.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a rounded numeric value.

For example:

round(125.678, 2)

Result:

125.68

docs.title: Decimal places
docs.text:
The decimalPlaces parameter determines the position to which the value is rounded:

  • a positive value — rounds to the specified number of decimal places;
  • 0 — rounds to the nearest integer;
  • a negative value — rounds to tens, hundreds, thousands, and other positions.

For example:

round(125.678, 0)

Result:

126

round(1896, -2)

Result:

1900

It is recommended to use integers for decimalPlaces. A fractional value may be converted when the result is calculated.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value and an expression

If the value field contains 2, the expression:

round(value + 10, 2)

returns:

12

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Both parameters are required.

For example:

round(125.678)

returns an error.

An error also occurs if one of the parameters is empty:

round(emptyField, 2)

A text value cannot be used instead of a numeric value, even if the text contains a number:

round("125.678", 2)

also returns an error.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
Use roundup or rounddown when you need to round a value up or down.

  • round — rounds a number to the nearest value;
  • roundup — rounds a value up;
  • rounddown — rounds a value down.

docs.title: rounddown
docs.text: The rounddown function rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places without increasing the last retained digit.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
rounddown(value, decimalPlaces)

Parameters:

  • value — the numeric value to round. Required;
  • decimalPlaces — the number of decimal places to round to. Required.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a rounded numeric value.

For example:

rounddown(125.678, 2)

Result:

125.67

When rounding to two decimal places, the retained digits 67 remain unchanged.

docs.title: Decimal places
docs.text:
The decimalPlaces parameter determines the position to which the value is rounded:

  • a positive value — rounds to the specified number of decimal places;
  • 0 — rounds to an integer;
  • a negative value — rounds to tens, hundreds, thousands, and other positions.

For example:

rounddown(1896, -2)

Result:

1800

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value and an expression

If the value field contains 125.678, the expression:

rounddown(value + 10, 2)

returns:

135.67

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
Different rounding methods are available:

  • round — rounds a number to the nearest value;
  • roundup — increases the last retained digit when rounding;
  • rounddown — keeps the last retained digit unchanged.

docs.title: roundup
docs.text: The roundup function rounds a number to the specified number of decimal places, increasing the last digit of the result.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
roundup(value, decimalPlaces)

Parameters:

  • value — the numeric value to round. Required;
  • decimalPlaces — the number of decimal places to round to. Required.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a number rounded away from zero.

For example:

roundup(125.671, 2)

Result:

125.68

docs.title: Decimal places
docs.text:
The decimalPlaces parameter determines the position to which the value is rounded:

  • a positive value — rounds to the specified number of decimal places;
  • 0 — rounds to an integer;
  • a negative value — rounds to tens, hundreds, thousands, and other positions.

For example:

roundup(1891, -2)

Result:

1900

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
For positive numbers, the result is rounded up to the nearest value with the specified number of decimal places.

For negative numbers, rounding is also performed away from zero:

roundup(-125.671, 2)

Result:

-125.68

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value and an expression

If the value field contains 125.671, the expression:

roundup(value + 10, 2)

returns the result rounded away from zero to two decimal places.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
Different rounding methods are available:

  • round — rounds a number to the nearest value;
  • roundup — rounds a number away from zero;
  • rounddown — rounds a number toward zero.

docs.title: capFirst
docs.text: The capFirst function makes the first letter of a string uppercase and converts all remaining letters to lowercase.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
capFirst(expression)

Parameters:

  • expression — a text value or expression that returns a string. In the function settings, this parameter is Expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns a string value with the letter case changed.

docs.title: Formatting text
docs.text:
Expression:

capFirst("GENERAL MANAGER")

returns:

General manager

docs.title: Formatting a field value
docs.text:
Suppose the position field contains:

HEAD OF LEGAL DEPARTMENT

Expression:

capFirst(position)

returns:

Head of legal department

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: If expression returns a value of another type, the function returns an error.

docs.title: contains
docs.text: The contains function checks whether a string contains a specified substring. It can be used in conditions where document generation depends on the presence of certain text in a value.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
contains(String, Substring, Match case)
  • String — required. The source string in which the search is performed.
  • Substring — required. The sequence of characters to search for within the string.
  • Match case — optional Boolean parameter. Determines whether the comparison is case-sensitive.

If Match case is omitted, the comparison is case-sensitive by default.

To perform a case-insensitive search, pass false as the third argument.

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
The function returns a Boolean value:

  • True — the specified substring is found in the string.
  • False — the specified substring is not found in the string.

The returned value can be used in conditions and other expressions.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: If Substring is empty, the function returns true.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Suppose the PaymentTerms field contains the following value:

Payment is due within 10 business days after delivery of the goods

Check whether the field value contains DELIVERY, ignoring case:

contains(PaymentTerms, "DELIVERY", false)

Result:

true

Since the third argument is set to false, differences in letter case do not affect the result.

docs.title: endsWith
docs.text: The endsWith function checks whether a string ends with a specified substring. It can be used in conditions where document generation depends on the ending of a text value.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
endsWith(String, Substring, Match case)
  • String — required. The source string whose ending is to be checked.
  • Substring — required. The sequence of characters that must match the end of the string.
  • Match case — optional Boolean parameter. Determines whether the comparison is case-sensitive.

If Match case is omitted, the comparison is case-sensitive by default.

To perform a case-insensitive comparison, pass false as the third argument.

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
The function returns a Boolean value:

  • True — the string ends with the specified substring.
  • False — the string does not end with the specified substring.

The returned value can be used in conditions and other expressions.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: If Substring is empty, the function returns true.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Check whether the string ends with AGREEMENT, ignoring case:

endsWith("Supply agreement", "AGREEMENT", false)

Result:

true

Since the third argument is set to false, differences in letter case do not affect the result.

docs.title: find
docs.text:
The find function searches for a specified fragment in a string and returns the position where it begins.

The function is useful when the position of the required text is not known in advance. The returned position can be used in other functions, such as mid, to extract a specific part of a string.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
find(string, substring, [startPosition], [matchCase])

Parameters:

  • string — the value in which to search. Required;
  • substring — the text or character to find. Required;
  • startPosition — the position from which to start the search. Optional. By default, the search starts from the first character;
  • matchCase — determines whether the search is case-sensitive. Optional. By default, the search is case-insensitive.

You can use text, field values, results of other functions, and expressions as parameters.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
If the specified fragment is found, the function returns the position of its first character. Counting starts from 1.

For example:

find("Acme Company", "Com", 1, false)

Result:

6

If the specified text is not found, the function returns null.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Finding a character in a field value

If the documentNumber field contains:

Contract No.125/2026

the expression:

find(documentNumber, "No.")

returns the position where No. begins.

Extracting text after a found fragment

You can pass the result of find to mid when you need to extract a part of text whose position is not known in advance.

For example:

mid(
    documentNumber,
    find(documentNumber, "No.") + length("No."),
    length(documentNumber)
)

If documentNumber contains:

Contract No.125/2026

the result is:

125/2026

Here, find determines the position of No., while length("No.") moves the starting position to the first character after it. The length function allows the remaining text to be extracted through the end of the string.

Searching from a specific position

If the same fragment appears more than once, you can start the search from a specified position instead of the first character:

find(text, "/", 10)

In this case, the function searches for / starting from the tenth character of the string.

Case-sensitive search

Set matchCase to true when the letter case must match:

find("Contract CONTRACT", "CONTRACT", 1, true)

The function searches for the substring using the exact letter case.

docs.title: length
docs.text: The length function counts the number of characters in text, a number, or a field value.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
length(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the value for which the number of characters should be determined. Required.

You can use text, a field value, the result of another function, or an expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the number of characters as a number. Letters, digits, spaces, and other characters are all included in the count.

For example:

length("New contract")

Result:

12

If you pass an empty string or a field with no value, the function returns 0.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value

If the name field contains:

Kombinator

the expression:

length(name)

returns:

10

Using with another function

length is often used together with mid when you need to extract part of a text value through the end of the string:

mid(documentNumber, 5, length(documentNumber))

If documentNumber contains:

DOC-125/2026

the result is:

125/2026

docs.title: lower
docs.text: The lower function converts all letters to lowercase.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
lower(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the value in which the letter case should be changed. Required.

You can use text, a field value, the result of another function, or an expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns text with all letters converted to lowercase. Numbers, spaces, and other characters are not changed.

For example:

lower("NEW CONTRACT NO. 15")

Result:

new contract no. 15

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using a field value

If the name field contains:

COMMERCIAL PROPOSAL

the expression:

lower(name)

returns:

commercial proposal

Changing the case of part of a text value

You can use lower together with mid when only part of a value should be converted to lowercase.

For example:

lower(mid(text, 2, length(text)))

If the text field contains:

KOMBINATOR

the result is:

ombinator

Together with upper, you can process the first letter and the remaining part of the text separately:

upper(mid(text, 1, 1)) & lower(mid(text, 2, length(text)))

If text contains:

kOMBINATOR

the result is:

Kombinator

docs.title: mid
docs.text:
The mid function extracts part of a text value starting from a specified position.

The function is useful when a single value contains several parts and you need to extract a specific fragment, such as a document number, code, detail, or text that follows a particular word.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
mid(text, position, length)

Parameters:

  • text — the source value from which part of the text should be extracted. Required;
  • position — the character position where the required fragment starts. Required. Counting starts from 1;
  • length — the number of characters to extract. Required.

You can use text, a field value, the result of another function, or an expression.

The position and length do not have to be specified as fixed numbers. You can calculate them using other functions, such as find and length.
